selected_evidence.requirement: AIDE installed and baseline database initialized for /etc integrity tracking
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed AIDE absent on RHEL 9.8 node1, installed aide-0.19.2, reviewed default /etc coverage, and ran aide --init producing a 39333-entry database.

selected_evidence.requirement: Config strengthened so content changes to /etc files are detected (not just permissions)
selected_evidence.summary: Changed the default catch-all '/etc PERMS' (metadata-only) rule to '/etc NORMAL' (adds sha512 content hashing) in /etc/aide.conf, backing up the original config first.

Installed the reinitialized database (post config change) to /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz and ran aide --check confirming 'AIDE found NO differences between database and filesystem. Looks okay!!' with 39334 entries.

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline proven to detect later changes to /etc files
selected_evidence.summary: Appended a line to /etc/motd and re-ran aide --check, which reported 'AIDE found differences between database and filesystem!!' with 'f > ... H.... : /etc/motd' showing the content-hash mismatch was detected.
Reverted /etc/motd, reran aide --init, installed the refreshed database, and confirmed a clean aide --check ('Looks okay!!', 39334 entries, sha256 4dcca975...).
Captured boot_id bef0e5ec-ce32-423b-826a-8a5a90584d3a and confirmed aide.db.gz sha256 4dcca975... plus aide service state prior to restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Issued systemctl reboot (acknowledgement returned), observed connection timeouts while the node was down, then reconnected and read a new boot_id 33a0bbf0-1f23-489f-975c-b29a564a4128, proving an actual restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of integrity baseline (data and function)
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz sha256 unchanged (4dcca975...) after reboot, and aide --check ran successfully reporting 'AIDE found NO differences between database and filesystem. Looks okay!!' with 39334 entries.
